PullRequest.Title: agentHost: run on-device models with llama.cpp
PullRequest.Body:

Adds on-device ("local") models to the Copilot Agent Host. A model from the Azure ML catalog (MAI Code 1.1 Flash today) is downloaded into the `~/.copilot/azureml-models` store shared with the Copilot CLI and app, and served by a `llama-server` the user provides. The whole feature is behind `chat.copilot.localModel.enabled`, which is off by default and tagged experimental.

No public issue yet.

## What changed

**Agent Host** (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/localModelBridge/`)
- **Catalog and downloads** (`modelCatalog.ts`, `downloader.ts`, `store.ts`): lists the Azure ML catalog anonymously, downloads with resume, retry and timeouts, and verifies every file's SHA-256 before use. It never deletes files it didn't create in the shared store.
- **llama.cpp** (`llamaCppRuntime.ts`): runs only the `llama-server` named by the `chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath` setting (machine-scoped, so a workspace can't set it) and checks its capabilities before use. VS Code never installs llama.cpp. Loading without a usable build shows how to get one, with *Get llama.cpp*, *Open Settings* and *Retry*.
- **Serving** (`serverSupervisor.ts`, `servingProfile.ts`, `gguf.ts`):
  - Picks a GPU memory profile and checks free memory before starting the server.
  - Starts and stops `llama-server` and recovers from crashes, falling back to plain decoding when speculative decoding fails.
  - Passes the server's API key through `LLAMA_API_KEY` rather than the command line. The server is only marked ready once it refuses unauthenticated requests.
  - Only NVIDIA GPUs where a model fits are offered.
- **Request routing** (`copilotRequestHandler.ts`, `requestRouter.ts`): a `CopilotRequestHandler` bridge.
  - **Direct selection:** served on the local server.
  - **Auto (off by default):** offers the loaded model to CAPI's `/auto` and serves a local pick, falling back to the cloud before the first output.
  - **Model swaps:** turns that are using the model keep it until they end, so a swap waits for them.
- **Runtime settings:** the Copilot runtime started by VS Code always gets `AUTO_LOCAL_ROUTING=false` and `WINML_LOCAL_MODELS=false`, so it never starts a second server.

**Workbench**
- **Model picker:** an *On This Device* tab. Each model has a detail page with Download, thinking level, context size (64K/128K/256K) and *Use in Auto*. Use in Auto shows the agreed local model safety disclosure. Models that aren't downloaded get a dimmed row with a Download action.
- **No modal dialogs or toasts:** loading, waiting for running responses, errors and downloads show in one notice above the chat input, with Cancel. Stop Now and Remove still ask for confirmation.
- **Labels:** replies served on the device are labelled *On-device*, e.g. `Auto (MAI Code 1.1 Flash · On-device)`.
- **Accessibility:** help content, ARIA labels and announcements are covered. The fixtures render in dark, light and both high-contrast themes.

## Things reviewers should know
- **Undocumented Azure ML endpoints** (`constants.ts`). The catalog search (`ai.azure.com/api/eastus/ux/v1.0/entities/crossRegion`) and lookup (`…/modelregistry/v1.0/registry/models/nonazureaccount`) are the anonymous backends of the Azure AI Foundry portal, the same ones the Copilot CLI uses. The documented Azure ML APIs need Azure sign-in.
  - The search only accepts User-Agents that start with `AzureAiStudio`, so we send `AzureAiStudio VSCode/<version>`.
  - This should get Azure ML's sign-off before the feature leaves preview.
- **Hardcoded requirements:** MAI's download size and GPU memory requirement aren't published on the asset yet. `UNPUBLISHED_REQUIREMENTS_FALLBACK` holds temporary values for exactly that version, matching the CLI's.
- **Auto never picks MAI yet:** VS Code offers the model to Auto, but in testing CAPI always chose a cloud model. That is decided on the CAPI side.
- **Shared model store:** the CLI's uninstall and stale-version cleanup can still delete versions VS Code downloaded. This needs coordination with the CLI and app.
- **Branch is behind main:** I'll merge main before marking this ready.
- **Suggested review order:**
  1. `common/localModel.ts` (protocol);
  2. `shim/shimLocalModelProvider.ts`;
  3. `shim/serverSupervisor.ts`;
  4. `shim/copilotRequestHandler.ts`;
  5. the workbench picker files.

## How to test
1. Use an NVIDIA GPU with enough memory for the model; MAI needs about 96 GiB.
2. Install a llama.cpp build that supports the model. MAI's `maion-coder` architecture needs [ggml-org/llama.cpp#29778](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29778).
3. Set `chat.copilot.localModel.enabled` to true and `chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath` to the build's `llama-server`.
4. In the chat model picker, open *On This Device* → the model → Download. When it's done, select it: the notice above the chat input shows the load with Cancel, then chat runs on the device.
5. Optionally, turn on *Use in Auto* on the detail page and select Auto.

Tested manually on Windows on Arm with an NVIDIA GPU and llama.cpp b11512, built with ggml-org/llama.cpp#29778:
- download and load, including speculative decoding;
- direct chat with the *On-device* label;
- Cancel while loading;
- swapping models mid-turn;
- the llama.cpp directions error with Retry;
- the API key only on the environment.

## Validation
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed, 0 errors |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed |
| `scripts\test.bat --run` on the 21 local-model bridge suites (`src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\localModelBridge\*.test.ts`) | 274 passing |
| `scripts\test.bat --run` on the 59 on-device test files (local-model bridge, Agent Host, picker, notice, settings and accessibility suites) | 2852 passing, 4 failing. The failures are `TabbedActionListWidget` layout timeouts that also fail when that file runs alone; none of its code changed in this PR. |
| `scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\providerIntegration\copilotLocalModel.integrationTest.ts` | 8 passing |
| `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>` | Clean |
| `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>` | Passed |
| `npm run stylelint` | Passed |
| Component fixtures (`localModelPickerRows`, `chatInputNotice`, `tabbedModelPicker`) | All render without errors |

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The client-wide installation, unconditional call path, full-body allocation, second copy, and pass-through reachability are explicit in the changed code. Exact milliseconds depend on prompt size and runtime internals, but the scaling mechanism and large-context trigger are not speculative.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full request-body bytes and duplicate Uint8Array-backed objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added read and copy are O(request-body size) on every model-layer HTTP request while the opt-in handler is installed; long-context agent prompts can contain tens or hundreds of thousands of tokens, and the cost repeats for every model call.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased request-dispatch latency plus avoidable allocation and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the Copilot client had no custom request handler and ordinary cloud/BYOK requests followed the SDK's normal forwarding path without this bridge first materializing and copying their complete bodies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With on-device models enabled, the client installs this handler globally; every relayed request now awaits bufferRequest before classification, including requests ultimately classified as passThrough. bufferRequest calls request.arrayBuffer(), and passThrough rebuilds the Request through toRequest(), whose body uses buffered.body.slice().
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 374 unconditionally executes `await bufferRequest(request)` before route classification for every request handled by the newly installed client-wide bridge.
Findings.Title: Avoid buffering every request before routing
Findings.Impact: An opted-in user sending a large ordinary cloud agent request must now fully read and copy the prompt body before fetch can begin. At large context sizes this adds critical-path latency and transient memory/GC pressure even when no local model or Auto routing is used.
Findings.Evidence: CopilotAgent installs the handler as the client's requestHandler at src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts:3274. This class states that every model-layer request is relayed through it, line 374 unconditionally buffers before routing, bufferRequest at lines 70-76 materializes the whole body, and toRequest at lines 80-87 clones it again. The passThrough branch still uses that rebuilt request, so the mechanism reaches ordinary cloud and unrelated BYOK traffic.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the original Request on the fast path and classify obvious pass-through traffic before materializing its body. Buffer only candidate Auto/local routes that need inspection or replay, and avoid `slice()` for one-shot forwarding; create additional copies only when a fallback/reissue actually requires them.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The direct-request call path, awaited benchmark, readiness ordering, token count, and timeout are explicit. Hardware determines the exact delay, but all direct cold starts necessarily pay nontrivial model-inference work that is unrelated to the user's prompt.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GPU model inference for an unrelated prompt and 32 generated tokens
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The benchmark is paid on every server cold start, including the first direct request after the 15-minute idle unload and subsequent crash/restart loads; its latency is TTFT plus generation of 32 tokens, bounded only by the 120-second warm-up timeout.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked first-response critical path for directly selected on-device models
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this feature, a direct chat did not start a local server or run this synthetic inference. Within the new start path, the server is already healthy and authenticated before this step and could otherwise admit the waiting direct request immediately.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every successful server start now awaits `_warmUp` before publishing `server: 'ready'`, regardless of whether Auto is enabled or the start was triggered by a direct request. `_warmUp` sends an unrelated greeting with `max_tokens: 32` and `cache_prompt: false`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 753 synchronously awaits the synthetic model completion on the universal start path before the newly added server can transition to ready.
Findings.Title: Skip the full Auto benchmark on direct-only starts
Findings.Impact: When a user directly selects an unloaded model, `ensureStarted` keeps their real prompt waiting while the model first processes and generates a separate 32-token completion. Even a model that just meets the configured 8 token/s Auto gate adds roughly four seconds of decode time plus TTFT; slower direct-capable configurations can wait up to the 120-second timeout.
Findings.Evidence: Direct requests call `serving.ensureStarted` in copilotRequestHandler.ts:799-808. A start reaches a healthy authenticated server before this hunk, but line 753 awaits `_warmUp`; readiness is not published until serverSupervisor.ts:813. The warm-up body sets `max_tokens: WARMUP_GENERATED_TOKENS` at line 1115, constants.ts defines that as 32 and the timeout as 120 seconds, and the result is primarily consumed by `passesAutoGate` for Auto eligibility.
Findings.Recommendation: Run the full 32-token performance benchmark only when `useInAuto` is enabled (or off the direct-request critical path). For direct-only starts, use at most a minimal health/speculative-decoding probe, then publish ready so the waiting user prompt can run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary cloud or unrelated BYOK model call after the user enables on-device models
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK sends every model-layer HTTP request through LocalModelCopilotRequestHandler; the handler fully buffers the body, classifies it, rebuilds a Request, and only then starts the existing proxy-aware network fetch. All buffering is on the request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward the model-layer HTTP request through proxyFetch or loopbackFetch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing outbound fetch per pass-through model call; fallback/reissue paths can intentionally issue a second CAPI request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SDK used its normal forwarding path without the PR's client-wide custom bridge or mandatory pre-forward body materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fetch cannot begin until the newly added full-body buffering and copy complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the complete Request body into an ArrayBuffer and copy it with Uint8Array.slice when rebuilding the request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once plus one full copy for every non-GET/HEAD request handled, including pass-through traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks dispatch and creates transient memory proportional to the prompt body.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Request-body bytes per model call, realistically large for 64K-256K-token agent contexts; concurrent model calls multiply transient retained bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No coalescing or limiter applies to request buffering. Each concurrent SDK request independently materializes and copies its full body before its own fetch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies; the read and copy repeat for every request, regardless of route or warm state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: global handler installation, unconditional buffering, pass-through reachability, and the second copy are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact body sizes and allocation behavior inside the SDK vary, but long-context agent prompts make multi-megabyte bodies realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression; submitted as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: First direct on-device prompt with the model unloaded, including after idle unload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request waits in ensureStarted; runtime capability resolution and launch-plan preparation complete, llama-server is spawned and polled healthy, API-key enforcement is checked, props are read, then a 32-token synthetic completion is awaited before ready is published and the user's actual prompt can acquire a slot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/stat llama-server and fingerprint adjacent dynamic libraries; read model preset/GGUF metadata as needed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded preparation pass per start; capability and metadata caches remove most repeat work when unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before spawn, but generally cache-backed after first use.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fresh llama-server device admission probe and one long-lived llama-server spawn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One device probe and normally one server spawn per cold start; bounded downgrade or port/auth retries can add spawns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to load the selected model before direct inference.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Loopback health polling, unauthenticated props probe, authenticated props read, and synthetic warm-up completion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several bounded loopback probes plus exactly one 32-token warm-up on a normal successful start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No synthetic local inference preceded a user's prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synthetic completion remains on the critical path even after the server is healthy and authenticated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cold start per first use, model swap, crash restart, or use after the 15-minute idle unload; benchmark time scales with model TTFT and 32/decode throughput.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Starts are sequenced and single-flight per plan. The direct request waits behind that serialized start; no user inference can overlap the benchmark because readiness is published afterward.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime capabilities and GGUF metadata are cached, reducing warm filesystem/subprocess work. Server idle unload discards the loaded process, so the fresh admission, spawn, health checks, and benchmark repeat.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct ensureStarted waits for start, start awaits warm-up, and ready is published only afterward.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GPU throughput varies; an eligible model at the minimum configured 8 tokens/s already spends about four seconds decoding, while slower direct-only configurations can approach the 120-second timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work latency regression; submitted as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: On-device model catalog discovery, setup, resume, and update
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial discovery probes the GPU/runtime and scans installed versions; stale catalog refresh performs anonymous search. Setup resolves one chosen version, checks files and architecture, downloads selected files sequentially, hashes each full file, atomically places them, commits the manifest, and may load the model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Azure ML search, resolve, blob listing/config/HEAD metadata, bounded GGUF range reads, and model-file GETs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm discovery uses the 24-hour cache. Cold setup uses one resolve GET, one listing GET, one config GET, one HEAD per selected file, bounded architecture range requests, then one sequential transfer per selected file; retries/renewals are bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No VS Code on-device model acquisition path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata resolution and all selected file transfers must finish before installation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan shared store, maintain owner/manifest records, stream files, hash every byte, rename atomically, and prune owned old versions on update
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Directory operations scale with installed families/versions; hashing and writes scale linearly with selected model bytes and run sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No model-store scan or model-byte hashing by this process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Download writes and checksum verification are required before commit; store discovery runs during opt-in initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is catalog pages (bounded), selected model files (normally preset plus primary and optional draft), and total model bytes (about 56.7 GB for the current offer).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog resolutions share a limiter of two. One model download is sequential across files and guarded by a per-family process lock; transfers implement backpressure and retry from partial files rather than burst concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog results and content facts persist for 24 hours; GPU/runtime capability is cached by topology and binary/library fingerprint; verified partials resume, but complete files are intentionally rehashed before reuse. Adopted-file hashes are cached by path, mtime, and size.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: boundary counts, sequential transfer policy, caches, lock, and retry limits are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size is bounded and currently small; download duration depends mainly on network/disk throughput for the 56.7 GB model.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: large work is user-triggered/required, bounded, resume-aware, cache-aware, and avoids concurrency bursts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Auto routing with a loaded on-device model and cloud fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A CAPI /auto request may be patched with the local offer; if selected, the handler leases the pinned generation and a nonblocking slot, sends to loopback, buffers only until first local output, and either commits local output or issues one cloud fallback before commitment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: CAPI /auto declaration and optional cloud fallback request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One /auto call; at most one fallback inference call for the traced local attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CAPI selected and served cloud models without this local declaration/fallback bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CAPI selection precedes model inference; fallback begins only before any local output is committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per locally selected Auto model call, bounded by available server slots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the inference critical path when Auto selects local; first-output timeout permits fail-open fallback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One route record per Auto session token (soft cap 1024); one local request per selected model call; a pre-output local failure adds one fallback request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Auto never queues for a model slot; it falls back when slots are full. llama-server slot count bounds local inference, while route records are leased and swept.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Route records are in memory, expire with a grace period, are capped, and are invalidated by account generation. Endpoint failures are temporarily down-marked. Loaded model state avoids cold starts until idle unload.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CAPI currently may rarely choose the local offer, so prevalence is uncertain; the route and concurrency mechanics are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond global request buffering; slot admission, route retention, and fallback cardinality are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Download/load progress displayed in chat input and model picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider progress recomputes status; the setup channel coalesces byte-only root-state publications to once per second; workbench observables update notifications and open picker rows, with notification progress mutated in place.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish local-model status through root transient values to connected agents/workbench
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Immediate for state-shape transitions; byte-counter-only progress is coalesced to at most one publication per second.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the download/server critical path; it reports progress asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update notification text/progress/actions and refresh an open picker list/detail card
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most about once per second for volatile progress, with in-place DOM updates when layout is stable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Renderer-side reporting only; does not block transfer or inference progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Duration of a download/load and number of visible chat inputs/picker instances; family collections are expected to remain small.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces provider-to-workbench progress. UI updates execute on the renderer thread but do not spawn parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Status observables use structural equality; picker state signatures ignore volatile byte counters and schedule progress refreshes at most once per second. No cold/warm cache distinction beyond widget/controller creation on first opt-in picker use.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous rendered chat inputs varies, but update frequency is explicitly coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff contains explicit IPC and UI coalescing and avoids rebuilding stable progress DOM.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 132-file inventory, all production paths relevant to subprocess, IPC, filesystem, network, serialization, cache/lifecycle, and UI rendering, plus focused tests. Submitted two findings: global full-body buffering/copying for all opt-in model requests, and a 32-token Auto benchmark blocking every direct cold start. Download, catalog, serving concurrency, cleanup, status IPC, and picker updates are bounded or coalesced and did not justify further findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
